judged_text: The sync fetch never checks response.ok and sets no timeout or error handling, so a 4xx/5xx body from the endpoint is returned to callers and parsed as a token payload. A parent-app outage or misconfiguration surfaces as cryptic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" errors (or persisted garbage) across every synced app's booking path, and a hung endpoint stalls bookings until the fetch times out — the diff adds a hard runtime dependency on the parent app in the booking hot path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), the “sync” path does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw `Response` without checking `response.ok`, without parsing JSON, and without any timeout/abort. Multiple call sites then treat the returned value as a token payload (or an axios/gaxios-style response): e.g. GoogleCalendarService does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` and then dereferences `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`—but a WHATWG `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and this will throw at runtime when syncing is enabled. Similar type/behavior mismatches exist in other integrations (e.g. Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object but would receive a `Response`). Separately, returning non-OK responses and/or hanging requests directly into the booking/token-refresh hot path matches the finding’s concern: errors surface as generic parse failures (e.g. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`) and there is no timeout handling in the diff.
